layers.basics: To control something, first write equations for it: a motor, a heater, a circuit. Electrical and mechanical systems have direct analogies.
layers.deeper: Mass–spring–damper ↔ series RLC; DC motor couples electrical and mechanical equations through k_t and k_e.
layers.expert: Force–voltage analogy; linearisation about operating point; state variables chosen as energy-storage quantities.

ext.title: Control Tutorials for MATLAB and Simulink

title: Transfer functions, block diagrams and signal-flow graphs

layers.basics: Block diagrams show how signals flow through subsystems; transfer functions in blocks multiply along a path.
layers.deeper: Closed-loop T=G/(1+GH); signal-flow graphs and Mason’s gain formula handle complex loops.
layers.expert: Mason: T=ΣPₖΔₖ/Δ, Δ=1−ΣL+ΣLL−…; block reduction rules; algebra equals Cramer’s rule on the graph.

title: Time-domain response: rise time, overshoot, settling time, steady-state error
summary: How a control system’s response is judged.

layers.basics: We judge a controller by how fast, how smoothly and how accurately the output follows a step command.
layers.deeper: Second-order metrics: overshoot %OS=e^{−πζ/√(1−ζ²)}, settling t_s≈4/(ζω_n), rise time ≈1.8/ω_n.
layers.expert: Steady-state error from system type: e_ss=1/(1+K_p) for type 0 step; type-1 systems track steps with zero error.

layers.basics: A table built from the characteristic polynomial’s coefficients reveals how many roots lie in the unstable right half-plane.
layers.deeper: Sign changes in the first column count unstable poles; handy for finding the gain at which a system goes unstable.
layers.expert: Special cases (zero in first column, row of zeros) handled by ε-substitution and auxiliary polynomial; gives critical K for oscillation.

title: Root locus
summary: How poles move as gain changes.

layers.basics: A root locus plots where the closed-loop poles go as the controller gain is turned up.
layers.deeper: Rules for sketching: starts at open-loop poles, ends at zeros, asymptotes, breakaway points.
layers.expert: Angle condition ∠L(s)=±180°(2k+1), magnitude gives K; design by adding poles/zeros (compensators) to reshape locus.

layers.basics: Nyquist plots the open-loop response in the complex plane; encirclements of −1 reveal instability. Gain and phase margins show the safety buffer.
layers.deeper: Can be measured on real plants without a model; handles time delay.
layers.expert: Nyquist: Z=N+P; sensitivity peak M_s=max|1/(1+L)|; Bode gain–phase relation; delay adds phase −ωτ.

title: PID controllers

layers.basics: PID looks at the error now (P), its accumulated past (I) and its trend (D) to decide the correction; it runs most industrial loops.
layers.deeper: P speeds response, I removes steady error, D adds damping; tuning methods: Ziegler–Nichols, loop-shaping.
layers.expert: u=K_p e+K_i∫e+K_d de/dt; anti-windup, derivative filter; digital form with sample time; 2-DOF structures.

formula: u = Kp e + Ki ∫e dt + Kd de/dt

layers.basics: A lead compensator adds phase near crossover for stability and speed; a lag improves low-frequency gain (accuracy).
layers.deeper: Lead: C=(1+sαT)/(1+sT), α<1; lag: places a pole–zero pair at low frequency.
layers.expert: Max phase lead φ_m=asin((1−α)/(1+α)) at ω=1/(T√α); lead-lag combined = PID-like.

title: State-space methods

layers.basics: State-space writes a system as first-order equations in a state vector; it handles multi-input multi-output systems naturally.
layers.deeper: ẋ=Ax+Bu, y=Cx+Du; eigenvalues of A are the poles; transfer function G=C(sI−A)⁻¹B+D.
layers.expert: Realisations (canonical forms); similarity transformations; balanced truncation for model reduction.

formula: ẋ = Ax + Bu;  y = Cx + Du

title: Controllability and observability
summary: Can we steer it? Can we see it?

layers.basics: Controllable: inputs can drive the state anywhere. Observable: outputs reveal the state.
layers.deeper: Rank tests on the controllability matrix [B AB … Aⁿ⁻¹B] and the observability matrix.
layers.expert: Kalman decomposition; duality; PBH test; uncontrollable modes cannot be moved by feedback.

layers.basics: State feedback u=−Kx can set closed-loop poles anywhere if the system is controllable; observers estimate unmeasured states.
layers.deeper: Ackermann’s formula; Luenberger observer; separation principle lets you design them separately.
layers.expert: LQR minimises ∫(xᵀQx+uᵀRu), solved via Riccati equation; LQG = LQR + Kalman filter.

layers.basics: Digital controllers sample the plant, compute in software, and output through a DAC with zero-order hold.
layers.deeper: Discretise the plant (c2d) or the controller (Tustin); choose sample rate ≥10× bandwidth.
layers.expert: z-plane stability inside unit circle; deadbeat; computational delay and jitter; aliasing; dual-rate loops.
